chunks: There is in the heavens your sustenance, and whatever has been promised you.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'your sustenance is in the heavens'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the divine guarantee of rizq, linking material provision with the spiritual certainty of the Hereafter as promised by Allah. It reflects the belief that sustenance is not merely a physical necessity but a sign of God's ongoing care, reinforcing the trust (tawakkul) believers place in divine decree. The mention of 'what you are promised' connects earthly sustenance with the ultimate reward of Paradise, a theme central to Shia eschatological hope.
